1.1: After Moses, the Lord's servant, passed away, the Lord spoke to Joshua, son of Nun, who had been Moses' right-hand man.
1.2: He said, 'Moses, my servant, gone now. It's your time. Get up, cross this Jordan River, you and all these people, and step into the land I'm giving y'all—the Israelites.'
1.3: 'Everywhere y'all step, I already gave it to you, just like I promised Moses.'
1.4: 'From the desert to Lebanon, from the big Euphrates River—where all them Hittites live—all the way to the Great Sea in the west, that's all your territory now.'
1.5: 'Ain't nobody gon' be able to step to you your whole life. Just like I was with Moses, I'm gon' be with you. I ain't never gon' leave you or turn my back on you.'
1.6: 'Be strong, hold your head high, and walk with courage. You gon' be the one to divide this land up for the people, just like I promised their ancestors.'
1.7: 'But for real, be strong and super courageous. Make sure you do everything in the law Moses gave you. Don't veer off—left or right—so you can move wisely wherever you go.'
1.8: 'Keep this book of the law on your mind, talk about it, think on it day and night. Live by what's in it, and you gon' be prosperous and successful in all you do.'
1.9: 'Ain't I told you already? Be strong, be brave. Don't be shook or stressed, cause the Lord your God is rolling with you wherever you go.'
1.10: Then Joshua told the officers of the people,
1.11: 'Go through the camp and tell everybody, 'Get your stuff ready, cause in three days, we crossing this Jordan to take the land the Lord your God is giving us to own.''
1.12: Then Joshua hollered at the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh,
1.13: 'Y'all remember what Moses, the Lord's servant, told you: 'The Lord your God is giving you rest and this land.''
1.14: 'Your wives, kids, and livestock can stay in the land Moses gave y'all on this side of the Jordan, but all y'all mighty warriors gotta strap up and go help your brothers claim their land.'
1.15: 'Once the Lord gives them rest like He gave y'all, and they got their land, then y'all can come back and settle in the land Moses gave you on this side of the Jordan, east of the sunrise.'
1.16: The people told Joshua, 'We got you. Whatever you tell us, we'll do. Wherever you send us, we'll go.'
1.17: 'Just like we listened to Moses, we listening to you. Only thing we ask is that the Lord your God stay with you like He was with Moses.'
1.18: 'Anybody who acts up and don't listen to your orders, or goes against what you say, they gotta go. But for real, Joshua, be strong and stay courageous.'

2.1: Then Joshua, son of Nun, sent out two men from Acacia Grove on the low, tellin' them, 'Go scope out the land, especially Jericho.' So they went and ended up at the house of a woman named Rahab, who was known to host folks, and they stayed there.
2.2: But word got to the king of Jericho, 'Yo, some Israelite men came in here tonight to check out the land and see what's up.'
2.3: So the king sent messengers to Rahab, sayin', 'Bring out the men that came to your house. We know they in here trying to spy on the whole country.'
2.4: But Rahab had already hidden them, so she told the king's men, 'Yeah, they was here, but I ain't know where they was from.'
2.5: 'Right when the gate was closin' at night, they dipped. I don't know where they went, but if y'all hurry, you might still catch them.'
2.6: (But for real, she had already took them up to the roof and hid them under some stalks of flax she had stacked up.)
2.7: So the king's men took off down the road toward the Jordan, looking for them. As soon as they left, they shut the city gate behind them.
2.8: Later that night, before the men went to sleep, Rahab went up to the roof to talk to them.
2.9: She told them, 'Look, I already know the Lord done gave y'all this land. Everybody round here scared stiff because of y'all.'
2.10: 'We heard how the Lord dried up the Red Sea when y'all came out of Egypt. And how y'all took down them two Amorite kings on the other side of the Jordan—Sihon and Og—y'all wiped them out completely.'
2.11: 'As soon as we heard all that, our hearts dropped. Ain't nobody got no courage left to fight y'all, cause the Lord your God? He the real one, running heaven and earth.'
2.12: 'So I'm asking y'all, since I showed y'all love, swear to me in the Lord's name that y'all gon' do the same for my family. Give me a sign that you for real.'
2.13: 'Promise me y'all gon' spare my father, my mama, my brothers, my sisters, and everything they got. Don't let us die when y'all take over.'
2.14: The men told her, 'Bet. If you keep quiet about what we doing, we got you. When the Lord hands this place over to us, we gon' make sure you and yours are straight.'
2.15: Then Rahab let them down through her window with a rope, cause her house was built into the city wall.
2.16: She told them, 'Y'all gotta hit the mountains quick so y'all don't run into the king's men. Lay low for three days till they give up and come back, then y'all can go on your way.'
2.17: The men told her, 'Aight, but here's the deal—we only gotta keep this promise if you follow these instructions.'
2.18: 'When we come back to take the land, you need to tie this red cord in the same window you let us down through. Also, make sure your whole family—your folks, your siblings, everybody—is inside your house.'
2.19: 'If anybody steps outside that door into the streets, that's on them. But if somebody come in your house and lay hands on your people, that's on us.'
2.20: 'But if you snitch on us, this deal is off, and we ain't gotta keep our word.'
2.21: Rahab said, 'Aight, bet. I'll do exactly what y'all said.' Then she let them go, and as soon as they left, she tied the red cord in the window.
2.22: The spies took off to the mountains and hid out for three days. The king's men was out there searching everywhere but couldn't find them.
2.23: After that, the two men came down from the mountains, crossed back over the Jordan, and went straight to Joshua. They told him everything that happened.
2.24: They told Joshua, 'Yo, the Lord really put this land in our hands. Everybody over there scared to death cause of us.'

3.1: Early the next morning, Joshua got up, and they left Acacia Grove, heading toward the Jordan River. Him and all the Israelites camped there for the night before crossing over.
3.2: After three days, the leaders started moving through the camp,
3.3: Telling the people, 'When y'all see the priests, the Levites, carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord, that's your signal—it's time to move. Follow it.'
3.4: 'But keep a good distance—about two thousand cubits away—don't get too close. That way, y'all can see where you supposed to go, cause this ain't a path y'all been down before.'
3.5: Then Joshua told the people, 'Y'all need to get right and prepare yourselves, cause tomorrow the Lord gon' do some crazy wonders among us.'
3.6: Then Joshua told the priests, 'Pick up the ark of the covenant and lead the way across the Jordan.' So they picked it up and went ahead of the people.
3.7: Then the Lord spoke to Joshua, 'Today is the day I start putting you on the map in front of all Israel, so they know for sure that just like I was with Moses, I'm with you too.'
3.8: 'Tell the priests carrying the ark, 'When y'all get to the Jordan's edge, stand still in the water.''
3.9: So Joshua told the Israelites, 'Aight, come close and listen to what the Lord your God gotta say.'
3.10: Joshua said, 'This how y'all gon' know that the living God is right here with us and gon' clear out all these folks before us—the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites.'
3.11: 'Look, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is going ahead of y'all into the Jordan.'
3.12: 'So pick one man from each tribe of Israel—twelve in total.'
3.13: 'And here's what's gon' happen: the moment the priests carrying the ark step into the Jordan, the water gon' stop flowing. The river gon' stack up like a wall.'
3.14: So when the people packed up to cross the Jordan, the priests carrying the ark of the covenant led the way.
3.15: Now, the Jordan River was overflowing cause it was harvest season. But as soon as the priests' feet hit the edge of the water,
3.16: The water coming down from upstream stopped, piling up way far back at a town called Adam, near Zaretan. Meanwhile, the water flowing down to the Dead Sea completely dried up, so the people could cross the river right in front of Jericho.
3.17: The priests holding the ark of the covenant stood firm in the middle of the river on dry ground while all Israel walked across. Every last one of them got to the other side safe before the priests moved.

4.1: After everybody made it across the Jordan, the Lord spoke to Joshua, sayin':
4.2: 'Pick twelve men from the people—one from each tribe.'
4.3: 'Tell 'em to grab twelve stones from right where the priests are standin' in the middle of the Jordan. Y'all gon' carry 'em with you and set 'em down where y'all camping tonight.'
4.4: So Joshua called up the twelve men he had chosen from the Israelites—one from each tribe.
4.5: He told them, 'Go back to where the ark of the Lord is in the middle of the Jordan. Each of y'all grab a stone and put it on your shoulder, one for each tribe of Israel.'
4.6: 'This gon' be a sign for y'all. One day, when your kids ask, 'What's up with these stones?''
4.7: 'Tell 'em how the Lord stopped the Jordan River when the ark of the covenant crossed through. These stones are gon' be a reminder forever of what God did for us.'
4.8: So the Israelites did exactly what Joshua told them. They took twelve stones from the Jordan, just like the Lord had told Joshua, and carried 'em to the camp, setting 'em down there.
4.9: Joshua also set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, right where the priests holding the ark had stood. And they still there to this day.
4.10: The priests stood in the middle of the Jordan until everything was done—just like the Lord had told Joshua, just like Moses had said. The people didn't waste no time; they hurried and crossed over.
4.11: After everybody was across, the priests carrying the ark of the Lord came out too, in front of all the people.
4.12: The warriors from Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh's tribe crossed over armed and ready, just like Moses had told them to do.
4.13: About forty thousand soldiers marched across, ready for battle, heading to the plains of Jericho.
4.14: That day, the Lord put Joshua on a whole new level in front of all Israel. From then on, they respected him just like they did Moses, all the days of his life.
4.16: 'Tell the priests carrying the ark of the covenant to come up out of the Jordan.'
4.17: So Joshua gave the order, 'Come up out of the river!'
4.18: And as soon as the priests' feet hit dry ground, the water rushed back to where it was before, overflowing the banks like usual.
4.19: The people crossed the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, then set up camp at Gilgal, east of Jericho.
4.20: Joshua took those twelve stones they pulled from the Jordan and set 'em up in Gilgal.
4.21: Then he told the Israelites, 'One day, when your kids ask, 'What these stones mean?''
4.22: 'Tell 'em, 'This is where Israel crossed the Jordan on dry land.''
4.23: 'Cause the Lord your God dried up the river for y'all to cross, just like He did with the Red Sea when we was coming out of Egypt.'
4.24: 'He did this so the whole world would know how powerful the Lord is, and so y'all would always respect and honor Him.'

5.1: When all the kings of the Amorites on the west side of the Jordan and all the Canaanite kings near the sea heard how the Lord dried up the Jordan River for the Israelites to cross, they got shook. Their courage was gone, and they ain't have no fight left in them.
5.2: Then the Lord told Joshua, 'Get you some flint knives and circumcise the Israelite men again.'
5.3: So Joshua made the knives and circumcised the men at the place they later called 'Hill of the Foreskins.'
5.4: Now here's why Joshua had to do this: All the men who left Egypt, the ones who were old enough to fight, had died in the wilderness during the journey.
5.5: All those who came out of Egypt had already been circumcised, but the ones born in the wilderness hadn't been.
5.6: The Israelites wandered forty years in the desert till all the old heads who left Egypt had died off cause they ain't listen to the Lord. The Lord had told them they wouldn't see the promised land—the land flowing with milk and honey—cause they ain't obey.
5.7: So now, their sons, the next generation, had to be circumcised cause nobody had done it while they were traveling.
5.8: After Joshua finished circumcising all the men, they stayed in the camp till they healed up.
5.9: Then the Lord told Joshua, 'Today, I've rolled away the shame of Egypt from y'all.' That's why that place is called Gilgal to this day.
5.10: While camped in Gilgal, the Israelites kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, on the plains of Jericho.
5.11: The day after Passover, they finally ate the food from the land—some unleavened bread and roasted grain, straight from the fields.
5.12: That same day, the manna stopped falling. From then on, they ate off the land of Canaan, no more manna from heaven.
5.13: One day, while Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him with a sword drawn. Joshua walked up to him and said, 'You with us or against us?'
5.14: The man answered, 'Nah, I'm neither. I'm the Commander of the Lord's army, and I just got here.'
5.15: Then Joshua fell on his face, worshipped, and asked, 'What's the word from the Lord for me, His servant?'
5.16: The Commander of the Lord's army told him, 'Take off your sandals, cause where you standing is holy ground.' And Joshua did exactly that.

6.1: Jericho was on full lockdown cause of the Israelites—nobody was coming in or going out.
6.2: Then the Lord told Joshua, 'Look, I already gave you Jericho, its king, and all its warriors.'
6.3: 'Here's what y'all gon' do: All the soldiers march around the city once a day for six days.'
6.4: 'Seven priests gon' carry seven rams' horn trumpets ahead of the ark. But on the seventh day, y'all gon' march around the city seven times, and the priests gon' blow the trumpets.'
6.5: 'When y'all hear that long blast from the rams' horns, that's when everybody gon' shout loud! The walls gon' fall flat, and everybody can charge straight in.'
6.6: So Joshua called up the priests and told them, 'Pick up the ark of the covenant. Seven priests gon' carry seven trumpets and walk ahead of it.'
6.7: Then he told the people, 'Move out! March around the city. The armed men go first, leading the way for the ark of the Lord.'
6.8: So just like Joshua said, the seven priests with the trumpets started marching, blowing their horns, while the ark of the covenant followed behind.
6.9: The armed men went ahead of the priests blowing the trumpets, and the rear guard followed behind the ark. The trumpets stayed blasting the whole time.
6.10: Joshua told the people, 'Stay quiet—don't shout, don't talk, not a word until the day I tell y'all to shout. Then let it out loud!'
6.11: So the ark of the Lord went around the city once, then they all went back to camp and spent the night there.
6.12: Early the next morning, Joshua got up, and the priests picked up the ark of the Lord again.
6.13: The seven priests carrying the trumpets went ahead, blowing them non-stop, while the armed men marched in front and the rear guard followed the ark.
6.14: On the second day, they marched around the city once again, then went back to camp. They did this for six days.
6.15: On the seventh day, they got up at dawn and marched around the city seven times, just like before. This was the only day they did seven laps.
6.16: On the seventh lap, the priests blew their trumpets, and Joshua told the people, 'Shout! Cause the Lord done gave you this city!'
6.17: 'The whole city is set to be destroyed by the Lord, except Rahab and her family cause she hid our spies.'
6.18: 'Don't mess with none of the cursed stuff in the city, or you gon' bring trouble on all of Israel.'
6.19: 'All the silver, gold, bronze, and iron belong to the Lord's treasury—don't take none of it for yourself.'
6.20: When the priests blew the trumpets, the people shouted loud! As soon as they did, the walls of Jericho fell flat. Everybody rushed in and took the city.
6.21: They wiped out everything—men, women, kids, even the animals—nobody was spared.
6.22: Then Joshua told the two spies, 'Go to Rahab's house and bring her and her family out, just like we promised her.'
6.23: So the young men went in and brought out Rahab, her family, and everything she owned. They kept them safe outside the Israelite camp.
6.24: Then the Israelites burned down the whole city and everything in it. The only things they kept were the silver, gold, bronze, and iron, which went into the Lord's treasury.
6.25: But Rahab and her whole family got spared. She stayed living with the Israelites ever since, cause she hid the spies Joshua had sent to Jericho.
6.26: Then Joshua made a declaration: 'Anybody who tries to rebuild Jericho is cursed! They gon' lose their firstborn when they lay the foundation, and their youngest when they set up the gates.'
6.27: The Lord was with Joshua, and word about him spread everywhere across the land.

7.1: But Israel messed up—somebody took stuff they wasn't supposed to. Achan, son of Carmi, grandson of Zabdi, great-grandson of Zerah from the tribe of Judah, took some of the banned goods. And the Lord was heated at Israel for it.
7.2: Joshua sent some men from Jericho to Ai, near Beth Aven, east of Bethel, and told them, 'Go check out the land.' So they went and spied on Ai.
7.3: When they came back, they told Joshua, 'Ain't no need for everybody to go fight—just send two or three thousand men. Ai ain't got that many people; no need to wear everybody out.'
7.4: So about three thousand men went up, but they got whooped and had to retreat.
7.5: Ai's men chased them down from the city gate all the way to Shebarim, cutting down about thirty-six of them. The Israelites' courage vanished—they was shook.
7.6: Joshua tore his clothes, fell facedown in front of the ark of the Lord, and stayed there till evening. The elders of Israel did the same, throwing dust on their heads.
7.7: Joshua said, 'Lord God, why You even bring us over the Jordan if we just gon' get handed over to the Amorites and wiped out? We shoulda just stayed on the other side!'
7.8: 'Lord, what am I supposed to say now that Israel ran from their enemies?'
7.9: 'If the Canaanites and the rest hear about this, they gon' come for us, wipe us out, and then what's gon' happen to Your great name?'
7.10: The Lord told Joshua, 'Get up! Why you on the ground like that?'
7.11: 'Israel messed up bad—they broke My covenant. Somebody stole from what was set apart, lied about it, and hid it in their stuff.'
7.12: 'That's why Israel lost—they got cursed things among them. I ain't ridin' with y'all no more unless you clean house and get rid of it.'
7.13: 'Get up and tell the people: 'Get right for tomorrow, cause the Lord says there's something cursed in the camp. Y'all ain't gon' win another fight till it's gone.''
7.14: 'Tomorrow morning, all the tribes gon' come forward one by one, then the Lord gon' call out the guilty tribe. Then the families gon' step forward, then households, then man by man till the one who did this is found.'
7.15: 'Whoever got the cursed stuff gon' be burned up with everything they own, cause they disrespected the Lord and did Israel dirty.'
7.16: So Joshua got up early and had Israel come tribe by tribe. The Lord picked Judah.
7.17: Then He picked the clan of the Zarhites, then from them, He chose Zabdi's family.
7.18: Then one by one, He narrowed it down till Achan—son of Carmi, grandson of Zabdi, from Judah—was caught.
7.19: Joshua told Achan, 'Son, don't play with me. Give God His glory, come clean, and tell me what you did. Don't hide it.'
7.20: Achan answered, 'I ain't gon' lie—I messed up. I sinned against the Lord.'
7.21: 'I saw this fresh Babylonian robe, two hundred shekels of silver, and a gold bar worth fifty shekels. I wanted 'em bad, so I took 'em. They buried in my tent, with the silver underneath.'
7.22: Joshua sent some men to check, and sure enough, the stash was buried in Achan's tent with the silver underneath.
7.23: They grabbed the stolen goods, brought them back to Joshua and all Israel, and laid it out before the Lord.
7.24: Then Joshua and all Israel took Achan, the silver, the robe, the gold, his sons, his daughters, his cattle, donkeys, sheep, his tent, and everything he had, and dragged them to the Valley of Achor.
7.25: Joshua said, 'Why you bring trouble on us? Now the Lord bringin' trouble on you!' Then all Israel stoned them, then burned them up.
7.26: They piled a huge heap of stones over him, which is still there today. After that, the Lord's anger cooled down. That's why that place is called the Valley of Achor to this day.

8.1: Then the Lord told Joshua, 'Don't be scared or discouraged. Take all your warriors and go hit Ai. I already gave you the king, the people, the city, and the land.'
8.2: 'You gon' do Ai the same way y'all did Jericho and its king, but this time, y'all can keep the goods and livestock for yourselves. Set up an ambush behind the city.'
8.3: So Joshua and his army got ready to go against Ai. He picked thirty thousand strong warriors and sent them out at night.
8.4: He told them, 'Y'all gon' hide behind the city, not too far, and be ready.'
8.5: 'Me and the rest gon' roll up on the city. When they see us, they gon' chase us, thinking we running away like last time.'
8.6: 'They gon' leave the city wide open, thinking they got us. That's when we dip, acting like we scared.'
8.7: 'Then y'all gon' rush in, take the city, cause the Lord already handed it to us.'
8.8: 'Once y'all take it, burn it down. This is what the Lord told us to do.'
8.9: Joshua sent them out, and they went to hide between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of the city, while he stayed with the rest of the people overnight.
8.10: Early in the morning, Joshua got everybody ready, and him and the elders led them up to Ai.
8.11: The whole army moved in, camping north of Ai, with a valley between them and the city.
8.12: Then Joshua had another five thousand men hide between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.
8.13: With the army set up on both sides, Joshua went into the valley that night.
8.14: When the king of Ai saw them, he rushed out early in the morning with all his people, ready to fight. But he ain't know there was an ambush waiting behind the city.
8.15: Joshua and his army faked like they was losing and started running toward the wilderness.
8.16: All the men of Ai got hyped, came out the city, and chased after them, leaving the whole city wide open.
8.17: Ain't a single man left inside Ai or Bethel—they was all chasing Israel, thinking they had the upper hand.
8.18: Then the Lord told Joshua, 'Point your spear at Ai, cause I'm giving it to you now.' So Joshua stretched out his spear toward the city.
8.19: As soon as he did, the ambush squad jumped up, ran into the city, took it over, and set it on fire.
8.20: When the men of Ai turned around, they saw their city up in smoke. They had nowhere to run, cause Israel had them surrounded.
8.21: Once Joshua and his men saw the ambush team had taken Ai and set it on fire, they turned back and attacked the men of Ai.
8.22: The Israelites trapped them on both sides and wiped them out—nobody escaped.
8.23: They caught the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.
8.24: After Israel finished taking out all Ai's people in the field and the wilderness, they went back into the city and finished the job.
8.25: That day, twelve thousand people—every last person in Ai—got taken out.
8.26: Joshua kept holding his spear up till everybody in Ai was destroyed.
8.27: But Israel kept the livestock and the city's goods, just like the Lord told Joshua.
8.28: Then Joshua burned Ai to the ground and left it as ruins, a wasteland forever.
8.29: He had the king of Ai hanged on a tree till evening. When the sun set, Joshua had his body taken down, thrown at the city gate, and covered with a big pile of stones—still there to this day.
8.30: Then Joshua built an altar to the Lord, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal.
8.31: He did it just like Moses had commanded, using whole stones that nobody had ever cut with iron tools. Then they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to the Lord.
8.32: There, in front of the Israelites, Joshua wrote down the whole law of Moses on stones.
8.33: Then all of Israel—leaders, officials, judges, and even the foreigners among them—stood on both sides of the ark of the covenant. Half stood in front of Mount Gerizim, the other half in front of Mount Ebal, just like Moses had told them to do.
8.34: Then Joshua read every word of the law, the blessings and the curses, exactly as it was written in the Book of the Law.
8.35: Not a single word Moses had commanded was left out—Joshua read it all to the whole assembly, including the women, kids, and foreigners living with them.

9.1: When all the kings west of the Jordan—up in the hills, in the valleys, and along the coast near Lebanon—heard what went down, including the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites,
9.2: They all teamed up, ready to go to war against Joshua and Israel.
9.3: But when the people of Gibeon heard what Joshua did to Jericho and Ai,
9.4: They got slick with it—they planned a scheme and acted like they was ambassadors. They loaded up old sacks on their donkeys, brought busted wineskins that had been patched up,
9.5: Wore raggedy sandals, dusty clothes, and brought dried-up, moldy bread like they been traveling for months.
9.6: They pulled up to Joshua at Gilgal and told him and the Israelites, 'We from a faraway land—let's make a deal, a covenant.'
9.7: But the Israelites was suspicious, saying, 'How we know y'all ain't just some locals tryna finesse us? We ain't supposed to make no covenant with folks living around here.'
9.8: The Gibeonites told Joshua, 'We your servants.' But Joshua wasn't buying it yet. He asked, 'Who are y'all, and where y'all really from?'
9.9: They said, 'We came from way far off cause we heard about the Lord your God—how He been handling business, what He did in Egypt,'
9.10: 'And how He took out Sihon, king of Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan, over in Ashtaroth.'
9.11: 'So our leaders told us, 'Pack up, take some supplies, and go meet them. Tell them we your servants—make a deal with them.''
9.12: 'Look at this bread—it was fresh when we left, now it's all dried up and nasty.'
9.13: 'These wineskins? Brand new when we filled 'em, now they torn up. Our clothes and sandals? Straight up falling apart from all this traveling.'
9.14: The Israelites checked out their supplies, but they ain't bother to ask God what to do.
9.15: So Joshua made peace with them, set up a covenant letting them live, and the Israelite leaders swore on it.
9.16: But three days later, Israel found out the truth—the Gibeonites wasn't from no faraway land, they was neighbors, living right there.
9.17: So Israel went to check out their cities—Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kirjath Jearim—on the third day.
9.18: But they couldn't attack them, cause the leaders had already sworn an oath to them in the Lord's name. The whole community started complaining to the leaders about it.
9.19: The leaders told the people, 'We swore in the Lord's name—we can't go back on it now.'
9.20: 'Here's what we gon' do—we let them live, cause if we break our oath, we gon' bring down the Lord's wrath on us.'
9.21: 'But they gotta work for us now—they gon' be cutting wood and carrying water for the whole community, just like we promised.'
9.22: Then Joshua called the Gibeonites and said, 'Why y'all lie to us? Saying you from far away when you right next door?'
9.23: 'Now y'all cursed—you and your people gon' be stuck as servants, cutting wood and hauling water for the house of my God forever.'
9.24: The Gibeonites replied, 'We knew for sure that the Lord your God told Moses to give y'all this land and wipe everybody out. We was scared for our lives, so we did what we had to do.'
9.25: 'Now we in your hands—do whatever you think is right to us.'
9.26: So Joshua let them live and made sure Israel didn't kill them.
9.27: But from that day forward, the Gibeonites became the permanent woodcutters and water carriers for Israel and the altar of the Lord, just like Joshua said. And they still doing that to this day.

10.1: Adoni-Zedek, king of Jerusalem, heard how Joshua took Ai and wiped it out—just like he did Jericho and its king—and how Gibeon had made peace with Israel and was now rollin' with them.
10.2: This had him shook, cause Gibeon was a big city, like one of the royal towns, even bigger than Ai, and its men were some real warriors.
10.3: So Adoni-Zedek sent word to Hoham, king of Hebron, Piram, king of Jarmuth, Japhia, king of Lachish, and Debir, king of Eglon, saying,
10.4: 'Come help me out! We gotta hit Gibeon, cause they switched sides and joined Joshua and Israel.'
10.5: So the five Amorite kings—the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon—linked up, brought their armies, and camped outside Gibeon, ready for war.
10.6: The Gibeonites sent word to Joshua at Gilgal, saying, 'Yo, don't leave us hanging! Come quick, help us out! All these Amorite kings from the hills teamed up against us!'
10.7: So Joshua and his whole army, including his best warriors, rolled out from Gilgal.
10.8: The Lord told Joshua, 'Don't be scared of them—I already gave 'em to you. Not a single one of them gon' stand against you.'
10.9: Joshua and his army marched all night from Gilgal and pulled up on them unexpectedly.
10.10: The Lord threw the enemy into total confusion. Israel put in work, killing them all over Gibeon, chasing them down the road toward Beth Horon, and striking them down all the way to Azekah and Makkedah.
10.11: While they was running away, the Lord started throwing down giant hailstones from the sky all the way to Azekah. More of them died from the hail than from Israel's swords.
10.12: That day, when the Lord handed the Amorites over to Israel, Joshua called on the Lord in front of everybody and said: 'Sun, stop right over Gibeon! Moon, stay put in the Valley of Aijalon!'
10.13: And the sun stopped, and the moon stood still until Israel got their payback on their enemies. Ain't this written in the Book of Jasher? The sun stayed in place in the sky and didn't go down for nearly a whole day.
10.14: Ain't never been another day like that before or after, where the Lord actually listened to a man like that—cause the Lord Himself was out there fighting for Israel.
10.15: Then Joshua and his army headed back to their camp at Gilgal.
10.16: Meanwhile, them five kings ran off and hid in a cave at Makkedah.
10.17: Somebody told Joshua, 'We found them kings hiding in a cave at Makkedah.'
10.18: Joshua said, 'Roll some big stones over the cave entrance and post guards there.'
10.19: 'But don't just stand around—chase down their troops, attack their rear guard, and don't let them make it back to their cities, cause the Lord already handed them over to us.'
10.20: So Joshua and the Israelites kept wiping them out until barely any of them were left. The few who got away made it into fortified cities.
10.21: When the Israelites came back to camp at Makkedah, everybody was safe—nobody even dared to talk trash against them.
10.22: Then Joshua said, 'Open up that cave and bring those five kings out here.'
10.23: So they pulled out the five kings—the ones from Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.
10.24: Joshua called his army captains and told them, 'Come here and put your foot on these kings' necks.' So they stepped up and did it.
10.25: Then Joshua told them, 'Don't be scared or weak—be strong and stand tall. This what the Lord gon' do to every enemy you fight.'
10.26: Then Joshua killed them and had them hanged on five trees, where they stayed till evening.
10.27: At sunset, Joshua ordered their bodies to be taken down, thrown into the cave they hid in, and sealed it with big rocks. That spot still like that to this day.
10.28: That same day, Joshua took Makkedah, killed the king and everybody in it—didn't leave nobody alive. He did Makkedah's king just like he did Jericho's.
10.29: Then Joshua and the Israelites rolled out to Libnah and went to war.
10.30: The Lord gave Libnah into Israel's hands—they took out the king, killed everyone in the city, and left no survivors, just like Jericho.
10.31: From Libnah, Joshua led the army to Lachish, set up camp, and attacked.
10.32: The Lord gave Lachish over to Israel on the second day, and they wiped out the whole city, just like Libnah.
10.33: When Horam, king of Gezer, came to help Lachish, Joshua and his army took him out too—nobody was left alive.
10.34: Then they moved to Eglon, set up camp, and went to war.
10.35: That same day, they took the city, wiped out everybody in it, and left no survivors—just like they did to Lachish.
10.36: From Eglon, Joshua and the Israelites went up to Hebron and attacked.
10.37: They took it, killed the king, and wiped out every single person—no survivors, just like they did to Eglon.
10.38: Then Joshua led the army to Debir and attacked.
10.39: They took the city, its king, and all the surrounding towns, killing everybody in it. No survivors. Joshua handled Debir just like he did Hebron, Libnah, and Jericho.
10.40: Joshua conquered the whole region—the mountains, the desert, the lowlands, the slopes—took out every king, left no survivors, wiping out everything that breathed, just like the Lord commanded.
10.41: He took them down from Kadesh Barnea all the way to Gaza, covering Goshen to Gibeon.
10.42: Joshua took down all these kings and their lands in one go, cause the Lord Himself was fighting for Israel.
10.43: Then Joshua and the whole army headed back to their camp at Gilgal.

11.1: When Jabin, king of Hazor, heard about all this, he sent word to Jobab, king of Madon, and to the kings of Shimron and Achshaph,
11.2: And to all the kings up north—in the mountains, the plains near Chinneroth, the lowlands, and the high places near Dor in the west,
11.3: To the Canaanites in the east and west, the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, and Jebusites in the mountains, and the Hivites down near Mount Hermon in Mizpah.
11.4: All these kings gathered their armies—a massive crowd, as many as the sand on the shore. They had a crazy amount of horses and chariots.
11.5: They all linked up and camped at the waters of Merom, ready to go to war against Israel.
11.6: But the Lord told Joshua, 'Don't even trip about them. By this time tomorrow, I'm handing them all over to Israel—dead. You gon' hamstring their horses and burn up their chariots.'
11.7: So Joshua and his whole army pulled up on them at the waters of Merom, caught them slipping, and attacked.
11.8: The Lord gave Israel the victory—they chased them all the way to Greater Sidon, to the Brook Misrephoth, and to Mizpah Valley in the east, striking them down until nobody was left.
11.9: Just like the Lord told him, Joshua took out their horses' legs and set their chariots on fire.
11.10: Then Joshua turned back and took Hazor, killed its king, cause Hazor used to be the head of all these kingdoms.
11.11: They took out everybody in the city—every last one, no survivors. Then they burned Hazor to the ground.
11.12: Joshua went through all the cities of these kings, took them out, and wiped them out, just like Moses had commanded.
11.13: But Israel didn't burn down any other cities except Hazor.
11.14: They took all the wealth and livestock for themselves, but they killed every person, leaving no one alive.
11.15: Joshua did everything just like the Lord commanded Moses. He followed every instruction, leaving nothing undone.
11.16: So Joshua took all the land—the mountains, the southlands, Goshen, the lowlands, and the Jordan Valley. He conquered the mountains of Israel and their surrounding lands,
11.17: From Mount Halak near Seir all the way to Baal Gad in Lebanon Valley below Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings, took them out, and executed them.
11.18: Joshua was at war with these kings for a long time.
11.19: Not a single city made peace with Israel, except the Hivites from Gibeon. Everybody else had to get handled in battle.
11.20: The Lord made sure their hearts stayed hardened so they would fight Israel and get wiped out. He didn't let them get mercy—just like He told Moses.
11.21: At that time, Joshua also went after the Anakim—the giants in the mountains—from Hebron, Debir, Anab, and all over Judah and Israel. He wiped them out and tore down their cities.
11.22: None of the Anakim were left in Israel, except for a few in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
11.23: So Joshua took the whole land, just like the Lord told Moses. Then he divided it among Israel's tribes as their inheritance. And finally, the land had peace—no more war.

12.1: These the kings Israel took down before they even crossed the Jordan—on the east side, from the River Arnon to Mount Hermon, covering all the eastern Jordan valley.
12.2: First was Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled from Heshbon. He controlled half of Gilead, from Aroer on the Arnon River all the way to the Jabbok River, which was the border of the Ammonites.
12.3: He also controlled the eastern Jordan valley, stretching from the Sea of Chinneroth to the Salt Sea, including the road to Beth Jeshimoth and the land south of Pisgah.
12.4: Then there was Og, king of Bashan, one of the last of the giants. He ruled from Ashtaroth and Edrei,
12.5: Covering Mount Hermon, Salcah, all of Bashan, up to the borders of the Geshurites and Maachathites, and half of Gilead, right up to Sihon's territory.
12.6: Moses, the Lord's servant, and Israel took them out, then gave their land to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half of Manasseh's tribe as their share.
12.7: Now these the kings that Joshua and Israel took down after crossing the Jordan—on the west side, from Baal Gad in Lebanon Valley all the way to Mount Halak near Seir. Joshua split up this land among the tribes.
12.8: This land covered mountains, valleys, plains, slopes, deserts, and the southern region—taking out the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
12.10: The king of Ai (next to Bethel)—one.
12.36: The king of Jokneam in Carmel—one.
12.37: The king of Dor (in the heights of Dor)—one.
12.38: The king of the people of Gilgal—one.
12.40: All together, Joshua and Israel took down 31 kings.

13.1: By this time, Joshua was getting old. The Lord told him, 'You up in age now, but there's still a lot of land left to take over.'
13.2: 'Here's what's left: all the land of the Philistines and the Geshurites,'
13.3: 'From Sihor, east of Egypt, up to Ekron in the north (which is counted as Canaanite land). This includes the five Philistine rulers—the ones over Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron—plus the Avites.'
13.4: 'From the south, all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah that belongs to the Sidonians, reaching to Aphek and the Amorite border.'
13.5: 'The land of the Gebalites and all of Lebanon, from Baal Gad under Mount Hermon to Hamath's entrance.'
13.6: 'Everybody in the mountains from Lebanon to the Brook Misrephoth, and all the Sidonians—I'll clear them out Myself. But you need to divide this land up for Israel, just like I commanded.'
13.7: 'Now go ahead and split it up as an inheritance for the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.'
13.8: The Reubenites and Gadites, along with the other half of Manasseh's tribe, already got their land on the east side of the Jordan—just like Moses, the Lord's servant, gave them.
13.9: From Aroer on the Arnon River, including the town in the middle of the valley, plus all the flatlands of Medeba as far as Dibon,
13.10: All the cities ruled by Sihon, king of the Amorites, who had Heshbon, stretching to the Ammonite border,
13.11: Gilead, the land of the Geshurites and Maachathites, Mount Hermon, and all of Bashan reaching to Salcah.
13.12: This included all of Og's kingdom in Bashan—he was one of the last giants. He ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei. But Moses took him out and claimed the land.
13.13: But Israel didn't clear out the Geshurites or Maachathites completely, so they still living among them to this day.
13.14: Only the Levites ain't get no land—cause the Lord's sacrifices were their inheritance, just like He said.
13.15: Moses gave the tribe of Reuben their land, divided by their families.
13.16: Their territory stretched from Aroer on the Arnon River, including the town in the valley and all the plains by Medeba,
13.17: Heshbon and all the cities in the flatlands—Dibon, Bamoth Baal, Beth Baal Meon,
13.19: Kirjathaim, Sibmah, Zereth Shahar in the valley hills,
13.20: Beth Peor, Pisgah's slopes, and Beth Jeshimoth,
13.21: All the cities in the plains, plus the whole kingdom of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled from Heshbon. Moses took him down along with the Midianite leaders—Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba—who were Sihon's officials.
13.22: Israel also took out Balaam, son of Beor—the sorcerer—when they handled Sihon's people.
13.23: Reuben's land stretched to the Jordan River. This was their inheritance—the cities and their surrounding villages.
13.24: Moses gave land to the tribe of Gad, divided by their families.
13.25: Their territory included Jazer, all the cities of Gilead, and half the Ammonite land up to Aroer, near Rabbah.
13.26: From Heshbon to Ramath Mizpah and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to Debir's border,
13.27: In the Jordan Valley—Beth Haram, Beth Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, plus the rest of Sihon's kingdom from Heshbon. The Jordan River marked their border up to the edge of the Sea of Chinnereth, on the east side of the Jordan.
13.28: This was Gad's inheritance—the cities and villages that came with it.
13.29: Moses also gave land to half the tribe of Manasseh, divided by their families.
13.30: Their land stretched from Mahanaim, covering all of Bashan and the whole kingdom of Og, including all sixty towns of Jair in Bashan.
13.31: It also included half of Gilead, plus Ashtaroth and Edrei—two major cities in Og's kingdom. This was for the descendants of Machir, son of Manasseh, split among his people.
13.32: These were the lands Moses gave out east of the Jordan, in the plains of Moab near Jericho.
13.33: But the Levites ain't get no land—cause the Lord God of Israel Himself was their inheritance, just like He said.

14.1: These the lands Israel inherited in Canaan, divided up by Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the tribes.
14.2: The land was handed out by casting lots, just like the Lord told Moses to do, for the nine and a half tribes.
14.3: Moses already gave land to the other two and a half tribes on the east side of the Jordan, but the Levites ain't get no land among them.
14.4: Since Joseph's descendants were split into two tribes—Manasseh and Ephraim—they still got their share. The Levites only got cities to live in, along with fields for their animals and crops.
14.5: Israel did just like the Lord told Moses, and they divided up the land.
14.6: Then the people of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb, son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, said, 'You remember what the Lord told Moses, the man of God, about me and you back in Kadesh Barnea?'
14.7: 'I was 40 years old when Moses sent me from Kadesh Barnea to spy on the land. I came back and gave him my honest take on it.'
14.8: 'But the other spies? They had everybody scared. Meanwhile, I stayed faithful to the Lord my God.'
14.9: 'So Moses made a promise that day: 'The land you walked on is yours forever, for you and your kids, cause you stayed faithful to the Lord.''
14.10: 'Now look—the Lord kept me alive just like He said, all these 45 years while Israel was out here wandering in the wilderness. Now I'm 85 years old.'
14.11: 'And I still got it. I'm just as strong now as I was when Moses sent me out—still got the strength to fight and handle business.'
14.12: 'So go 'head and give me that mountain the Lord promised back then. You know them Anakim giants live there, and their cities got big, strong walls. But with the Lord on my side, I'ma drive them out, just like He said.'
14.13: Joshua blessed Caleb and gave him Hebron as his inheritance.
14.14: So from that day on, Hebron belonged to Caleb, son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, cause he stayed true to the Lord God of Israel.
14.15: Hebron used to be called Kirjath Arba, named after Arba, the greatest of the Anakim giants. After that, the land finally had peace from war.

15.1: This the land given to the tribe of Judah, divided up by their families. Their southern border stretched to Edom at the Wilderness of Zin.
15.2: The southern border started at the shore of the Salt Sea, from the bay facing south.
15.3: Then it ran south past Akrabbim, through Zin, went up the south side of Kadesh Barnea, passed through Hezron, went up to Adar, and curved around to Karkaa.
15.4: From there, it stretched toward Azmon, followed the Brook of Egypt, and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. That was their southern border.
15.5: Their eastern border was just the Salt Sea, all the way up to the mouth of the Jordan River.
15.6: The northern border started at the bay of the Salt Sea at the Jordan's mouth, ran up to Beth Hoglah, passed north of Beth Arabah, and went up to the stone of Bohan, son of Reuben.
15.7: Then it ran up to Debir from the Valley of Achor, turned north toward Gilgal (before the Ascent of Adummim), then went toward the waters of En Shemesh and ended at En Rogel.
15.8: Then it climbed through the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, running past the south side of Jebusite city (which is Jerusalem). It continued to the top of the mountain overlooking Hinnom Valley from the west, at the north end of Rephaim Valley.
15.9: From there, it curved to the spring at Nephtoah, went to the cities on Mount Ephron, and circled around Baalah (Kirjath Jearim).
15.10: Then it turned west from Baalah to Mount Seir, ran past the north side of Mount Jearim (Chesalon), went down to Beth Shemesh, and passed Timnah.
15.11: Then it ran north past Ekron, curved around to Shicron, passed Mount Baalah, stretched to Jabneel, and ended at the Mediterranean Sea.
15.12: The western border was just the coastline of the Mediterranean. That was Judah's territory, divided up by their families.
15.13: Joshua gave Caleb, son of Jephunneh, a special share in Judah's land, just like the Lord commanded. He got Kirjath Arba (which is Hebron), named after Arba, the father of the Anakites.
15.14: Caleb pulled up and drove out the three Anakite brothers living there—Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
15.15: Then he marched on to Debir, which used to be called Kirjath Sepher.
15.16: Caleb said, 'Whoever takes this city can have my daughter Achsah as his wife.'
15.17: So Othniel, son of Kenaz (Caleb's younger brother), took the city, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as a wife.
15.18: When she got married, she told Othniel to ask her father for some land. She hopped off her donkey, and Caleb asked, 'What you need?'
15.19: She said, 'Since you gave me land in the South, bless me with some springs of water too.' So Caleb gave her both the upper and lower springs.
15.20: This was the inheritance of the tribe of Judah, divided by their families.
15.21: The cities near the southern border, by Edom, were: Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur,
15.25: Hazor, Hadattah, Kerioth, Hezron (also called Hazor),
15.32: Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon. Altogether, that's 29 cities with their villages.
15.33: In the lowlands: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah,
15.36: Sharaim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim. Fourteen cities with their villages.
15.41: Gederoth, Beth Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah. Sixteen cities with their villages.
15.44: Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah. Nine cities with their villages.
15.45: Ekron, with all its surrounding towns and villages.
15.46: From Ekron to the sea, everything near Ashdod, including its villages.
15.47: Ashdod with its towns and villages, and Gaza with its towns and villages—all the way to the Brook of Egypt and the Mediterranean coastline.
15.48: In the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, Socoh,
15.51: Goshen, Holon, and Giloh. Eleven cities with their villages.
15.54: Humtah, Kirjath Arba (which is Hebron), and Zior. Nine cities with their villages.
15.57: Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah. Ten cities with their villages.
15.59: Maarath, Beth Anoth, and Eltekon. Six cities with their villages.
15.60: Kirjath Baal (which is Kirjath Jearim) and Rabbah. Two cities with their villages.
15.61: In the desert region: Beth Arabah, Middin, Secacah,
15.62: Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En Gedi. Six cities with their villages.
15.63: But when it came to the Jebusites living in Jerusalem, Judah couldn't drive them out completely. So to this day, the Jebusites still live among the people of Judah in Jerusalem.

16.1: The land given to Joseph's descendants started from the Jordan River, near Jericho, stretching east to the waters of Jericho, then up through the mountains to Bethel.
16.2: From Bethel, it went to Luz, then to the border of the Archites at Ataroth.
16.3: From there, it went west, past the land of the Japhletites, down to Lower Beth Horon, then to Gezer, and finally ended at the sea.
16.4: So the two tribes from Joseph's line—Manasseh and Ephraim—got their inheritance.
16.5: Ephraim's land, divided by family, had its eastern border start at Ataroth Addar, stretching to Upper Beth Horon.
16.6: From there, the border went north of Michmethath, then curved east toward Taanath Shiloh, passing by Janohah on the east.
16.7: Then it dropped down from Janohah to Ataroth and Naarah, reached Jericho, and ended at the Jordan River.
16.8: The border went from Tappuah west to the Brook Kanah, finally ending at the sea. This was the land given to the Ephraimites, divided by their families.
16.9: Even though the Ephraimites had their own cities, some of their towns were mixed into Manasseh's land, all with their own villages.
16.10: But they ain't drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer. So the Canaanites still live among the Ephraimites to this day, working for them as forced laborers.

17.1: The tribe of Manasseh got their land too, since Manasseh was Joseph's firstborn. His firstborn son, Machir, who was the father of Gilead, was a warrior—so he got Gilead and Bashan.
17.2: The rest of Manasseh's people got their share too, based on their families: the clans of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. All these were the sons of Manasseh, Joseph's son.
17.3: But there was this one dude, Zelophehad—son of Hepher, grandson of Gilead, great-grandson of Machir, and part of Manasseh's tribe—who ain't have no sons, just daughters. His daughters' names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
17.4: They pulled up to Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the leaders and said, 'The Lord told Moses to give us a share of the land just like our brothers got.' So, following the Lord's command, Joshua gave them land among their uncles.
17.5: Manasseh ended up with ten portions of land, plus Gilead and Bashan on the other side of the Jordan.
17.6: This happened because Manasseh's daughters got an inheritance just like the sons, and the rest of the sons got Gilead.
17.7: Manasseh's land stretched from Asher to Michmethath, east of Shechem, and then south to the people of En Tappuah.
17.8: Manasseh owned the land of Tappuah, but the actual city of Tappuah, sitting on Manasseh's border, belonged to the Ephraimites.
17.9: The border ran down to the Brook Kanah. Some of Ephraim's cities were actually inside Manasseh's territory. Manasseh's land ran north of the brook and ended at the sea.
17.10: Ephraim's land was to the south, Manasseh's to the north, and the sea was their western border. Manasseh's land also touched Asher's land up north and Issachar's land to the east.
17.11: Inside Issachar and Asher's territories, Manasseh had control over Beth Shean and its towns, Ibleam and its towns, Dor and its towns, En Dor and its towns, Taanach and its towns, and Megiddo and its towns—all hilly regions.
17.12: But Manasseh's people couldn't kick out the Canaanites from those cities. The Canaanites were too determined to stay.
17.13: Later on, when Israel got stronger, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but they still didn't completely drive them out.
17.14: The descendants of Joseph came to Joshua and said, 'Why you only gave us one piece of land? We a big tribe! The Lord done blessed us, and we growing fast!'
17.15: Joshua told them, 'If y'all really that big, go clear out some land for yourselves in the forest country where the Perizzites and the giants live. Since the mountains of Ephraim ain't enough for you, expand out.'
17.16: But the people of Joseph said, 'That mountain land still ain't enough for us, plus the Canaanites in the valley got iron chariots! The ones in Beth Shean and the Valley of Jezreel? They too strong for us!'
17.17: Joshua told the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh, 'Listen, y'all a strong and powerful people. Y'all ain't just getting one share of land.'
17.18: 'That whole mountain country gon' be yours. Yeah, it's got forests now, but chop 'em down and take that land. You gon' push out the Canaanites, even if they got iron chariots and look strong.'

18.1: All the Israelites gathered at Shiloh and set up the meeting tent there. The land was now under their control.
18.2: But seven tribes still ain't got their share of land yet.
18.3: So Joshua asked them, 'How long y'all gon' sit around instead of claiming the land the Lord already gave you?'
18.4: 'Pick three men from each tribe, and I'll send them to go survey the land. They'll check it out, write everything down, and bring it back to me.'
18.5: 'They gon' divide it into seven sections. Judah gon' keep their land in the south, and Joseph's tribe gon' keep their land in the north.'
18.6: 'Y'all survey the land in seven parts and bring it back to me so we can cast lots before the Lord to divide it up fairly.'
18.7: 'The Levites ain't getting no land cause they got the Lord's priesthood instead. And Gad, Reuben, and half of Manasseh already got their land east of the Jordan, which Moses gave them.'
18.8: So the men got up and left to go survey the land. Joshua told them, 'Go walk through the land, write everything down, then come back so I can cast lots for y'all here in Shiloh before the Lord.'
18.9: The men went, mapped out the land in seven sections, wrote it all down in a book, and brought it back to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh.
18.10: Then Joshua cast lots in Shiloh before the Lord, dividing up the land among Israel based on their groups.
18.11: Benjamin's land was assigned by lot, and it ended up between the land of Judah and Joseph's descendants.
18.12: The northern border started at the Jordan River, stretched past Jericho on the north side, and ran west into the mountains, ending at the Wilderness of Beth Aven.
18.13: Then it went over to Luz (which is Bethel), headed south, then ran down to Ataroth Addar, near the hill by Lower Beth Horon.
18.14: Then the border turned west to the south side, running past the hill near Beth Horon and ending at Kirjath Baal (Kirjath Jearim), a city of Judah. That was the western border.
18.15: The southern border started at Kirjath Jearim, stretched west, and reached the spring of Nephtoah.
18.16: Then it went down the mountain at the edge of the Valley of Hinnom, which is north of the Rephaim Valley. It continued down to the Valley of Hinnom, near the Jebusite city (Jerusalem), and ran down to En Rogel.
18.17: From there, it turned north to En Shemesh, stretched to Geliloth (before the Ascent of Adummim), and went down to the stone of Bohan, son of Reuben.
18.18: Then it passed along the north side of Arabah and went down into Arabah.
18.19: The border kept going past the north side of Beth Hoglah and ended at the north bay of the Salt Sea, where the Jordan meets it in the south. That was the southern border.
18.20: The eastern border was the Jordan River. That's the land Benjamin got, with its boundaries mapped out for their families.
18.21: Benjamin's tribe got these cities: Jericho, Beth Hoglah, Emek Keziz,
18.24: Chephar Haammoni, Ophni, and Gaba—twelve cities with their villages.
18.28: Zelah, Eleph, Jebus (which is Jerusalem), Gibeath, and Kirjath—fourteen cities with their villages. This was the land given to Benjamin's tribe, split among their families.

19.1: The second lot went to Simeon's tribe, divided by their families. Their land was inside Judah's territory.
19.2: They got Beersheba (also called Sheba), Moladah,
19.6: Beth Lebaoth, and Sharuhen—13 cities with their villages.
19.7: They also got Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan—four cities with their villages.
19.8: Plus all the villages around these cities, reaching as far as Baalath Beer (also known as Ramah of the South). This was Simeon's inheritance, split up by families.
19.9: Simeon's land was inside Judah's because Judah had too much land, so Simeon got a piece of it.
19.10: The third lot went to Zebulun's tribe, divided by families. Their land stretched to Sarid.
19.11: Their border went west to Maralah, reached Dabbasheth, and followed the stream east of Jokneam.
19.12: From Sarid, it went east toward Chisloth Tabor, passed Daberath, and bypassed Japhia.
19.13: Then it ran east past Gath Hepher toward Eth Kazin and stretched to Rimmon, right by Neah.
19.14: Then it wrapped around the north side of Hannathon and ended at the Valley of Jiphthah El.
19.15: Their land included Kattath, Nahallal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem—12 cities with their villages.
19.16: That was Zebulun's inheritance, divided by families, including these cities and villages.
19.17: The fourth lot went to Issachar's tribe, divided by families.
19.18: Their land included Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem,
19.21: Remeth, En Gannim, En Haddah, and Beth Pazzez.
19.22: The border stretched to Tabor, Shahazimah, and Beth Shemesh, ending at the Jordan. They got 16 cities with their villages.
19.23: That was Issachar's inheritance, divided by families, including these cities and villages.
19.24: The fifth lot went to Asher's tribe, divided by families.
19.25: Their land included Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph,
19.26: Alammelech, Amad, and Mishal. It stretched west to Mount Carmel and the Brook Shihor Libnath.
19.27: It turned east toward Beth Dagon, reached Zebulun and the Valley of Jiphthah El, then went north past Beth Emek and Neiel, skirting Cabul on the left.
19.28: It included Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, reaching all the way to Greater Sidon.
19.29: Then it turned to Ramah and the fortified city of Tyre, before heading to Hosah and ending at the sea, near Achzib.
19.30: They also got Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob—22 cities with their villages.
19.31: That was Asher's inheritance, divided by families, including these cities and villages.
19.32: The sixth lot went to Naphtali's tribe, divided by families.
19.33: Their border started at Heleph, stretching past the terebinth tree at Zaanannim, through Adami Nekeb and Jabneel, reaching as far as Lakkum, where it ended at the Jordan.
19.34: From there, it extended west to Aznoth Tabor, then went toward Hukkok. It bordered Zebulun in the south, Asher in the west, and Judah at the Jordan in the east.
19.35: Their fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, and Chinnereth,
19.38: Iron, Migdal El, Horem, Beth Anath, and Beth Shemesh—19 cities with their villages.
19.39: That was Naphtali's inheritance, divided by families, including these cities and villages.
19.40: The seventh lot went to Dan's tribe, divided by families.
19.41: Their land included Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir Shemesh,
19.46: Me Jarkon, Rakkon, and the area near Joppa.
19.47: But Dan's people weren't satisfied with their land, so they went and fought against Leshem. They conquered it, wiped it out with the sword, took it over, and lived there. They renamed it Dan, after their ancestor.
19.48: That was Dan's inheritance, divided by families, including these cities and villages.
19.49: Once all the land had been divided up, the Israelites gave Joshua son of Nun his own share.
19.50: Following the Lord's command, they gave him the city he asked for—Timnath Serah in the mountains of Ephraim. He built up the city and lived there.
19.51: Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the tribal leaders divided up the land in Shiloh, at the entrance of the meeting tent, before the Lord. And that's how they finished dividing up the land.

20.1: Then the Lord spoke to Joshua, saying,
20.2: 'Tell the Israelites: Set up some cities of refuge, just like I told Moses.'
20.3: 'These cities gon' be safe spots for anybody who accidentally kills someone without meaning to. They can run there and be protected from anyone trying to get revenge.'
20.4: 'When they reach one of these cities, they gotta stand at the city gate and explain what happened to the elders. If it checks out, they'll let them in and give them a place to stay.'
20.5: 'If the person's being chased by someone looking for payback, the city can't hand them over—cause the killing wasn't on purpose, and there was no bad blood before it happened.'
20.6: 'They gotta stay in the city until they have a proper trial in front of the community. And they gotta stay there until the high priest of that time passes away. Then, they can go back home to their own city and house.'
20.7: So they set up these cities as refuges: Kedesh in Galilee, in Naphtali's mountains; Shechem in Ephraim's mountains; Kirjath Arba (which is Hebron) in Judah's mountains.
20.8: On the east side of the Jordan, near Jericho, they set up: Bezer in the wilderness, on the plains of Reuben's territory; Ramoth in Gilead, in Gad's territory; Golan in Bashan, in Manasseh's territory.
20.9: These cities were for all of Israel and any foreigners living with them—anyone who accidentally killed someone could flee there and stay safe until they had a fair trial, instead of being taken out by someone looking for revenge.

21.1: The leaders of the Levites came up to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of Israel's tribes.
21.2: They told them at Shiloh in Canaan, 'The Lord told Moses to give us cities to live in, plus land for our livestock.'
21.3: So, at the Lord's command, Israel gave the Levites cities and pastureland from their own shares.
21.4: The first lot went to the Kohathites. The descendants of Aaron (who were Levites and priests) got 13 cities from Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin's land.
21.5: The rest of Kohath's people got 10 cities from Ephraim, Dan, and half of Manasseh's land.
21.6: The Gershonites got 13 cities from Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and the other half of Manasseh's land in Bashan.
21.7: The Merarites got 12 cities from Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun's land.
21.8: Israel gave the Levites these cities and lands by casting lots, just like the Lord told Moses.
21.9: From Judah and Simeon's land, these cities were set aside for the Levites,
21.10: They went to Aaron's descendants, who were part of the Kohathite clan, since their lot came first.
21.11: They got Kirjath Arba (also called Hebron), in Judah's mountains. (Arba was the ancestor of the Anakites.) They also got all the pastureland around it,
21.12: But the fields and villages around Hebron were given to Caleb, son of Jephunneh, as his share.
21.13: The Levites got: Hebron (a city of refuge) and Libnah
21.16: Ain, Juttah, and Beth Shemesh. That's 9 cities from Judah and Simeon's land.
21.17: From Benjamin's land, they got: Gibeon and Geba
21.18: Anathoth and Almon. That's 4 cities in Benjamin.
21.19: In total, Aaron's descendants got 13 cities with their pasturelands.
21.20: Kohath's other Levite families got their share from Ephraim's land.
21.21: They received: Shechem (a city of refuge) and Gezer
21.22: Kibzaim and Beth Horon. That's 4 cities from Ephraim.
21.23: From Dan, they got: Eltekeh and Gibbethon
21.24: Aijalon and Gath Rimmon. That's 4 cities from Dan.
21.25: From half of Manasseh, they got: Tanach and Gath Rimmon. That's 2 cities from Manasseh.
21.26: In total, Kohath's remaining families got 10 cities with their pasturelands.
21.27: Gershon's Levites got land from the other half of Manasseh.
21.28: From Manasseh, they got: Golan in Bashan (a city of refuge) and Be Eshterah. That's 2 cities from Manasseh.
21.29: From Issachar, they got: Kishion and Daberath
21.30: Jarmuth and En Gannim. That's 4 cities from Issachar.
21.31: From Asher, they got: Mishal and Abdon
21.32: Helkath and Rehob. That's 4 cities from Asher.
21.33: From Naphtali, they got: Kedesh in Galilee (a city of refuge), Hammoth Dor, and Kartan. That's 3 cities from Naphtali.
21.34: In total, Gershon's Levites got 13 cities with their pasturelands.
21.35: Merari's Levites got their share from Zebulun's land.
21.36: From Zebulun, they got: Jokneam and Kartah
21.37: Dimnah and Nahalal. That's 4 cities from Zebulun.
21.38: From Reuben, they got: Bezer and Jahaz
21.39: Kedemoth and Mephaath. That's 4 cities from Reuben.
21.40: From Gad, they got: Ramoth in Gilead (a city of refuge) and Mahanaim
21.41: Heshbon and Jazer. That's 4 cities from Gad.
21.42: In total, Merari's Levites got 12 cities with their pasturelands.
21.43: In total, the Levites received 48 cities across Israel, with their pasturelands.
21.44: Each city had land surrounding it, just like the Lord commanded.
21.45: The Lord gave Israel all the land He promised to their ancestors. They took it and lived there.
21.46: The Lord gave them peace on all sides, just like He promised. None of their enemies could stand against them—God put them all in Israel's hands.
21.47: Not a single promise the Lord made to Israel failed. Everything came true.

22.1: Then Joshua called up the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh.
22.2: He told them, 'Y'all did everything Moses told you to do, and you listened to me every step of the way.'
22.3: 'For all this time, you ain't abandoned your brothers. You held it down and kept the Lord's command.'
22.4: 'Now the Lord has given peace to your people, just like He promised. So go on, head back to your tents, back to your land—the land Moses gave y'all on the other side of the Jordan.'
22.5: 'But listen, make sure you stay faithful. Follow the Lord's commands, love Him, walk in His ways, hold on tight to Him, and serve Him with all your heart and soul.'
22.6: Then Joshua blessed them and sent them home, and they went back to their tents.
22.7: Half of Manasseh's tribe got land in Bashan, while the other half got land west of the Jordan. Before they left, Joshua gave them a blessing too.
22.8: He told them, 'Go home with all these riches—livestock, silver, gold, bronze, iron, and clothes. And make sure you share the loot with your brothers.'
22.9: So Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh's tribe left Israel's camp at Shiloh in Canaan and went back home to Gilead, the land they got from the Lord through Moses.
22.10: When they got to the Jordan, the eastern tribes built a huge altar by the river.
22.11: But when the rest of Israel heard about it, folks started talking: 'Yo, did y'all hear? Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh just built an altar on our side of the Jordan!'
22.12: The whole congregation got heated and gathered at Shiloh, ready to go to war against them.
22.13: Israel sent Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest, to Gilead to talk to the eastern tribes.
22.14: They also sent ten tribal leaders, one from each tribe, all heads of their families in Israel.
22.15: They met with Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh in Gilead and told them,
22.16: 'What is this nonsense y'all just pulled? Why you rebelling against the Lord by building your own altar?'
22.17: 'Didn't we just recover from that mess at Peor? We still feeling the consequences of that sin!'
22.18: 'Now y'all wanna turn from the Lord again? You do this today, and tomorrow God's wrath gon' fall on all of us!'
22.19: 'Look, if your land ain't good enough, just move over to the Lord's land where the tabernacle is! But don't go making another altar and rebelling against God—and don't drag us into it!'
22.20: 'Y'all remember what happened to Achan, right? He sinned, and the whole nation suffered. This ain't just about you!'
22.21: Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh answered Israel's leaders and said,
22.22: 'The Lord God of gods, the Lord God of gods—He knows the truth. And Israel, y'all need to know it too. If we rebelled against God, then let Him deal with us right now.'
22.23: 'If we built this altar to go against the Lord, offer sacrifices, or start some mess—then may God punish us.'
22.24: 'But that ain't why we did it. We built it because we were worried about the future.'
22.25: 'We thought, What if later on, y'all start telling our kids: "Y'all ain't got no part in the Lord!"?'
22.26: 'So we built this altar not for sacrifices, but as a reminder to future generations.'
22.27: 'It's proof that we serve the Lord just like y'all do—that we bring offerings and sacrifices to the Lord, so nobody can ever say, "Y'all don't belong to God."'
22.28: 'If anybody ever tries to challenge us in the future, we'll just point to this altar and say, "This right here is proof that we follow the same Lord."'
22.29: 'Far be it from us to turn against the Lord! We ain't trying to make a separate altar for burnt offerings or sacrifices—there's only one altar, the Lord's altar, in front of the tabernacle.'
22.30: When Phinehas and the leaders heard their explanation, they relaxed. They saw it was all good.
22.31: Phinehas told them, 'Aight, now we see the Lord is still with us, cause y'all ain't committed no sin. Y'all just made sure Israel won't have beef down the road. That's a real win.'
22.32: So Phinehas and the leaders went back to Israel's camp in Canaan and gave their report.
22.33: Everybody in Israel was cool with it. They praised God and dropped all plans for war against Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh.
22.34: Reuben and Gad named the altar "Witness," saying, 'It stands as proof between us that the Lord is God.'

23.1: A long time passed after the Lord had given Israel peace from all their enemies. By then, Joshua was old and up in age.
23.2: So Joshua called all of Israel together—the elders, leaders, judges, and officers—and said to them:
23.3: 'Y'all saw with your own eyes what the Lord did to all these nations for you. It was the Lord fighting for you the whole time.'
23.4: 'I already divided up the remaining nations as your inheritance—from the Jordan to the Great Sea in the west, including the lands we took from defeated nations.'
23.5: 'And the Lord Himself gon' push the rest of them out. He gon' clear the way for y'all just like He promised.'
23.6: 'So be strong and make sure you follow everything written in the Book of the Law of Moses. Don't go left or right—stay on track!'
23.7: 'Don't start mixing with these nations still around you. Don't even mention their gods, don't swear by them, don't worship them, and don't bow down to them.'
23.8: 'Instead, stick tight to the Lord, just like you been doing till now.'
23.9: 'The Lord already drove out powerful nations before you, and nobody has been able to stand against you.'
23.10: 'One of y'all can chase a thousand, cause it's the Lord who fights for you—just like He promised.'
23.11: 'So stay on guard and make sure you love the Lord with everything you got.'
23.12: 'But if y'all turn back and start mixing with these nations, marrying them, and making alliances with them…'
23.13: 'Just know: The Lord ain't gon' push them out for you anymore. Instead, they gon' become traps, whips to your back, and thorns in your eyes—until y'all are completely wiped out from this land the Lord gave you.'
23.14: 'Look, today I'm about to leave this world like everybody else does. But y'all know deep down that every single promise the Lord made to you came true. Not one of them failed.'
23.15: 'But listen, just like the Lord kept His good promises, He gon' keep His warnings too. If y'all turn against Him, trouble is coming. Y'all will be destroyed from this good land He gave you.'
23.16: 'If you break the Lord's covenant and start serving other gods, bowing down to them, His anger gon' burn against you. And trust me, y'all gon' lose this land real quick.'

24.1: Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shechem. He called for the elders, leaders, judges, and officers, and they all stood before God.
24.2: Joshua told them, 'This what the Lord God of Israel says: 'Back in the day, your ancestors—including Terah, Abraham's and Nahor's daddy—lived on the other side of the river, and they worshiped other gods.'
24.3: 'But I took Abraham from across the river, led him all through Canaan, made his family big, and gave him Isaac.'
24.4: 'Then I gave Isaac two sons: Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the mountains of Seir to live in, but Jacob and his people ended up in Egypt.'
24.5: 'Then I sent Moses and Aaron and brought plagues on Egypt. After that, I pulled y'all out.'
24.6: 'When I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, they got chased down by Pharaoh's army with chariots and horsemen at the Red Sea.'
24.7: 'Y'all called out to Me, so I put darkness between y'all and the Egyptians, then drowned them in the sea. Y'all saw it with your own eyes. Then y'all wandered in the wilderness for a long time.'
24.8: 'I brought y'all into the land of the Amorites, and they fought against you. But I handed them over, so y'all could take their land. I wiped them out for y'all.'
24.9: 'Then Balak, king of Moab, tried to come for y'all. He sent for Balaam to curse you,'
24.10: 'But I didn't let Balaam curse you. Instead, he kept blessing y'all, and I saved you from him.'
24.11: 'Then y'all crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The people of Jericho fought against you—the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites—but I gave you the victory.'
24.12: 'I sent hornets ahead to chase them out—y'all ain't even need swords or bows for that.'
24.13: 'I gave y'all land you didn't work for, cities you didn't build, and vineyards and olive groves you didn't plant—and now y'all living off it.'
24.14: 'So now, fear the Lord and serve Him for real. Get rid of those fake gods your ancestors worshiped in Egypt and beyond the river. Serve the Lord!'
24.15: 'But if y'all don't wanna serve Him, then choose today who you gon' serve—the gods your ancestors had across the river, or the gods of the Amorites in this land. But as for me and my house, we serving the Lord!'
24.16: The people answered, 'Nah, we could never turn away from the Lord to serve other gods!'
24.17: 'The Lord is the one who brought us and our ancestors out of Egypt, out of slavery. He did miracles right in front of us, protected us on our journey, and kept us safe from our enemies.'
24.18: 'The Lord drove out all the people in this land before us, including the Amorites. We gon' serve the Lord too, cause He's our God!'
24.19: Joshua told them, 'Y'all can't serve the Lord like that, cause He's holy and jealous. He ain't gon' overlook y'all sins.'
24.20: 'If y'all turn away and start serving other gods, He gon' come for y'all. Just like He blessed you, He can take you out.'
24.21: But the people insisted, 'No! We gon' serve the Lord!'
24.22: Joshua said, 'Alright then, y'all are witnesses against yourselves that you chose to serve the Lord.'
24.23: 'Then get rid of those fake gods and give your full heart to the Lord God of Israel.'
24.24: The people replied, 'We gon' serve the Lord and listen to Him!'
24.25: So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day and set up rules in Shechem.
24.26: Then he wrote everything down in the Book of the Law of God. He also took a big stone and set it up under the oak tree by the Lord's sanctuary.
24.27: Joshua told the people, 'Look, this stone gon' be a witness against us. It heard everything the Lord said to us today. So don't play yourself and turn against Him.'
24.28: Then Joshua sent everybody back home to their own land.
24.29: After all this, Joshua son of Nun, the Lord's servant, died at 110 years old.
24.30: They buried him in his land at Timnath Serah, up in the mountains of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
24.31: Israel stayed faithful to the Lord as long as Joshua lived, and even after that, as long as the elders who knew about the Lord's miracles were still alive.
24.32: They also buried Joseph's bones at Shechem—the ones the Israelites brought from Egypt. They buried them on land that Jacob bought from Hamor's sons for 100 pieces of silver. That land became Joseph's descendants' inheritance.
24.33: Eleazar, son of Aaron, also died. They buried him in a hill that belonged to his son Phinehas, up in the mountains of Ephraim.
